## Using Templates When Sending [#using-templates-when-sending]

Reference a template by its `templateId` in the [Send Email](/api-reference/sending#send-email) or [Batch Send](/api-reference/sending#batch-send) content object:

```json
{
  "from": { "email": "hello@yourdomain.com" },
  "to": [{ "email": "alice@example.com" }],
  "content": {
    "templateId": "tmpl_e5f6g7h8"
  },
  "variables": {
    "first_name": "Alice",
    "order_id": "1234",
    "total": "$49.99"
  }
}
```

When `templateId` is provided, the template's subject, HTML, and text are used. The `subject` field in the content object is optional and overrides the template subject if provided.

## Template Variables [#template-variables]

Variables use Handlebars-style double-brace syntax: `{{variable_name}}`.

* Variable names are case-sensitive
* Unresolved variables are left as-is in the rendered output
* Variables work in the subject line, HTML body, and plain-text body
* In batch sends, per-recipient `variables` override top-level `variables`

### Template Object Reference [#template-object-reference]

| Field       | Type           | Description                                |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `id`        | string         | Unique template identifier                 |
| `name`      | string         | Internal template name                     |
| `subject`   | string         | Subject line with optional `{{variables}}` |
| `html`      | string \| null | HTML body                                  |
| `text`      | string \| null | Plain-text body                            |
| `variables` | string\[]      | Auto-extracted variable names              |
| `themeId`   | string \| null | Associated theme ID                        |
| `createdAt` | string         | ISO 8601 creation timestamp                |
| `updatedAt` | string         | ISO 8601 last update timestamp             |


# Webhooks



# Webhooks [#webhooks]

Webhook destinations must use HTTPS on port 443, without credentials in the URL, and resolve exclusively to public IP addresses. Private, loopback, link-local and reserved addresses are rejected on every delivery. Redirects are not followed; configure the final endpoint URL. Deliveries have a 10-second deadline. These rules apply to test deliveries too.

Webhooks deliver real-time HTTP POST notifications to your server when email events occur (delivery, bounce, open, click, etc.). Use webhooks to update your application state, trigger workflows, or monitor deliverability.

**Tier requirement:** Webhooks are available on Starter ($5/mo) and above: 1 endpoint on Starter, 3 on Micro, 10 on Pro, unlimited on Scale.

## Event Types [#event-types]

Subscribe a webhook to any of these values in `events`:

| Event                         | Description                                             | Trigger                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `email.queued`                | Message accepted and queued for delivery                | API, batch, scheduled or inbox send                                                                                  |
| `email.delivered`             | Email accepted by the recipient's mail server           | Successful SMTP delivery                                                                                             |
| `email.bounced`               | Email rejected by the receiving server                  | Bounce reported by the relay                                                                                         |
| `email.deferred`              | Email temporarily rejected; will retry                  | 4xx SMTP response                                                                                                    |
| `email.dropped`               | Message was not sent                                    | A batch or scheduled send failed, or a duplicate was discarded                                                       |
| `email.received`              | Inbound message received                                | Inbound mail to a hosted mailbox                                                                                     |
| `email.opened`                | A person opened the email (bots filtered)               | Tracking pixel loaded                                                                                                |
| `email.clicked`               | A person clicked a tracked link (bots filtered)         | Tracked link followed                                                                                                |
| `contact.subscribed`          | Someone subscribed, or opted back into a topic          | Signup form, Subscriptions API, list join, preference centre                                                         |
| `contact.confirmed`           | A double opt-in was confirmed                           | Recipient clicked the confirmation link                                                                              |
| `contact.unsubscribed`        | Someone unsubscribed from everything, a list or a topic | Unsubscribe link, one-click, preference centre, Subscriptions API                                                    |
| `list.member_added`           | A contact joined a list                                 | Subscriptions API, list member API, preference centre (signup forms report the list in `contact.subscribed` instead) |
| `list.member_removed`         | A contact left a list                                   | Unsubscribe from a list or topic, or removal by the list owner                                                       |
| `auth.success`, `auth.failed` | SMTP authentication events                              | Accepted in `events`; reserved for SMTP login notifications                                                          |

Payloads for the contact, list and engagement events are documented in [Contact, list and engagement events](#contact-list-and-engagement-events).

***

## List Webhooks [#list-webhooks]

Retrieve all configured webhook endpoints.

```
GET /webhooks
```

### Example Request [#example-request]

```bash
curl https://app.northrelay.ca/api/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer nr_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

### Example Response [#example-response]

```json
{
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "id": "cmg7w3bh00006qz8k9x8y7z6w",
      "url": "https://yourapp.com/webhooks/northrelay",
      "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "contact.unsubscribed"],
      "description": "Newsletter sync",
      "active": true,
      "secretPrefix": "whsec_AbC1De...",
      "totalDeliveries": 42,
      "createdAt": "2026-10-01T10:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-10-01T10:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

The full secret is never listed; only `secretPrefix`.

## Create Webhook [#create-webhook]

Register a new webhook endpoint.

```
POST /webhooks
```

### Request Body [#request-body]

| Field         | Type      | Required | Description                                        |
| ------------- | --------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`         | string    | Yes      | HTTPS endpoint URL that will receive POST requests |
| `events`      | string\[] | Yes      | One or more [event types](#event-types)            |
| `description` | string    | No       | Up to 500 characters                               |

### Example Request [#example-request-1]

```bash
curl -X POST https://app.northrelay.ca/api/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer nr_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://yourapp.com/webhooks/northrelay",
    "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "contact.unsubscribed"]
  }'
```

### Example Response [#example-response-1]

```json
{
  "webhook": {
    "id": "cmg7w3bh00006qz8k9x8y7z6w",
    "url": "https://yourapp.com/webhooks/northrelay",
    "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "contact.unsubscribed"],
    "description": null,
    "active": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-06T14:30:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-10-06T14:30:00.000Z",
    "secretPrefix": "whsec_AbC1De..."
  },
  "secret": "whsec_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "message": "Webhook created successfully. Save the secret - it will not be shown again."
}
```

Save the `secret` value -- you will need it to verify webhook signatures. The secret is only returned in the create response.

***

## Update Webhook [#update-webhook]

Update an existing webhook endpoint.

```
PATCH /webhooks/{id}
```

### Request Body [#request-body-1]

| Field         | Type      | Required | Description                   |
| ------------- | --------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `url`         | string    | No       | New endpoint URL              |
| `events`      | string\[] | No       | Updated event subscriptions   |
| `description` | string    | No       | Up to 500 characters          |
| `active`      | boolean   | No       | Enable or disable the webhook |

Returns `{ "webhook": { ... }, "message": "Webhook updated successfully" }`.

### Example Request [#example-request-2]

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://app.northrelay.ca/api/v1/webhooks/cmg7w3bh00006qz8k9x8y7z6w \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer nr_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "events": ["email.delivered", "email.bounced", "email.opened", "email.clicked", "contact.unsubscribed"],
    "active": true
  }'
```

## Delete Webhook [#delete-webhook]

Remove a webhook endpoint. No further events will be delivered.

```
DELETE /webhooks/{id}
```

### Example Request [#example-request-3]

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://app.northrelay.ca/api/v1/webhooks/cmg7w3bh00006qz8k9x8y7z6w \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer nr_live_xxxxxxxxxxxx"
```

### Example Response [#example-response-2]

```json
{ "message": "Webhook deleted successfully" }
```

## Get Webhook [#get-webhook]

```
GET /webhooks/{id}
```

Returns `{ "webhook": { ... }, "stats": { "totalDeliveries", "successfulDeliveries", "successRate" } }`, with delivery stats for the last 24 hours.

***

## Rotate Secret [#rotate-secret]

```
POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate
```

```json
{
  "id": "cmg7w3bh00006qz8k9x8y7z6w",
  "secret": "whsec_yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy",
  "previousSecretValidUntil": "2026-10-06T15:30:00.000Z"
}
```

The new secret is shown once. For one hour, until `previousSecretValidUntil`, deliveries also carry `X-NorthRelay-Signature-Previous`, signed with the old secret, so you can deploy the new secret without dropping events.

***

## Test Webhook [#test-webhook]

```
POST /webhooks/{id}/test
```

Sends a test event (body `{ "eventType": "<event type>" }`, default `email.delivered`) to an active webhook and reports the result:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "statusCode": 200,
  "responseTime": 184,
  "deliveryId": "5d0c6a1e-2b3f-4c7d-9e8a-1f2b3c4d5e6f",
  "message": "Test delivered (200) in 184ms"
}
```

When the endpoint cannot be reached, `success` is `false`, `statusCode` is `0` and `errorMessage` says why.

***

## SDK [#sdk]

```typescript
const { webhook, secret } = await client.webhooks.create({
  url: 'https://yourapp.com/webhooks/northrelay',
  events: ['contact.unsubscribed', 'list.member_removed', 'email.bounced'],
});
const { webhooks } = await client.webhooks.list();
const { webhook: current, stats } = await client.webhooks.get(webhook.id);
await client.webhooks.update(webhook.id, { active: false });
const rotated = await client.webhooks.rotateSecret(webhook.id);   // { id, secret, previousSecretValidUntil }
const test = await client.webhooks.testDelivery(webhook.id);
await client.webhooks.delete(webhook.id);
```

```python
from northrelay import CreateWebhookRequest, UpdateWebhookRequest

webhook = await client.webhooks.create(
    CreateWebhookRequest(url="https://yourapp.com/webhooks/northrelay", events=["contact.unsubscribed", "email.bounced"])
)
print(webhook.secret)  # shown once
await client.webhooks.update(webhook.id, UpdateWebhookRequest(active=False))
new_secret = await client.webhooks.rotate_secret(webhook.id)
await client.webhooks.delete(webhook.id)
```

See the [TypeScript SDK](/docs/sdks/typescript#webhooks) and [Python SDK](/docs/sdks/python#webhooks) for details.

***

## Payload Format [#payload-format]

Every webhook is an HTTP `POST` with a JSON body. All events share this envelope:

```json
{
  "eventType": "email.delivered",
  "messageId": "<20261006143500.a1b2c3@yourdomain.com>",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-06T14:35:00.000Z",
  "recipient": "alice@example.com",
  "sender": "hello@yourdomain.com",
  "subject": "Your order has shipped",
  "status": "delivered",
  "smtpResponse": "250 2.0.0 OK",
  "details": { }
}
```

| Field                        | Type   | Description                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `eventType`                  | string | One of the [event types](#event-types). Also sent in the `X-NorthRelay-Event` header.                                              |
| `messageId`                  | string | For `email.*` delivery events, the message id. For contact, list and engagement events, a unique id for this event.                |
| `timestamp`                  | string | ISO 8601 time the event was generated                                                                                              |
| `recipient`                  | string | Recipient (or contact) address, when there is one                                                                                  |
| `sender`                     | string | Sender address (`email.*` delivery events)                                                                                         |
| `subject`                    | string | Subject line (`email.*` delivery events)                                                                                           |
| `status`                     | string | Delivery status, for example `delivered` or `dropped`                                                                              |
| `smtpResponse`               | string | Response from the receiving server, when available                                                                                 |
| `bounceReason`, `bounceType` | string | Bounce details on `email.bounced` and `email.dropped`, when available                                                              |
| `details`                    | object | Event-specific data. For delivery events this is the raw event from the mail server; for the events below its shape is documented. |

Fields that do not apply to an event are omitted. Each request also carries `X-NorthRelay-Delivery` (a unique id per delivery attempt) and `X-NorthRelay-Signature`.

***

## Contact, List and Engagement Events [#contact-list-and-engagement-events]

These events let you keep your own application in sync with subscriptions and engagement. They fire for every path that changes a subscription: hosted signup forms, the [Subscriptions API](/docs/api-reference/subscriptions), list member changes, unsubscribe links, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribes and the hosted preference centre. CSV imports and direct contact edits (`POST` or `PATCH /contacts`) do not fire them.

### contact.subscribed [#contactsubscribed]

Someone subscribed, joined lists through a subscribe call, or opted back into a topic.

```json
{
  "eventType": "contact.subscribed",
  "messageId": "6f1c2a9e-4b7d-4f0e-9a51-2d3c8e7b1a40",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-06T14:02:11.000Z",
  "recipient": "jane@example.com",
  "details": {
    "contactId": "cmg7c0n1t0001qz8k2v5x9abc",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "source": "API",
    "listIds": ["cmg7l1st00002qz8kfe4w1xyz"],
    "topicIds": ["cmg7t0p1c0003qz8k7h2d4pqr"],
    "requiresConfirmation": true,
    "status": "PENDING"
  }
}
```

| `details` field              | Description                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contactId`, `email`         | The contact                                                                                          |
| `source`                     | `FORM`, `API`, `IMPORT`, `PREFERENCE_CENTER`, `PLATFORM_SIGNUP` or `DASHBOARD`                       |
| `listIds`                    | Lists the contact was asked to join (may be omitted or empty)                                        |
| `topicIds`                   | Topics the contact opted (back) into (may be omitted or empty)                                       |
| `requiresConfirmation`       | `true` while a double opt-in is outstanding; wait for `contact.confirmed`                            |
| `status`                     | Contact status after the change: `PENDING` or `ACTIVE`                                               |
| `formId`, `listId`, `fields` | Signup-form submissions only: the form, its list (kept for older consumers) and the submitted fields |

### contact.confirmed [#contactconfirmed]

The recipient clicked the double opt-in link.

```json
{
  "eventType": "contact.confirmed",
  "messageId": "0b8e3f52-1c6a-4d2e-8f7a-9e4b5c6d7a81",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-06T14:05:40.000Z",
  "recipient": "jane@example.com",
  "details": {
    "contactId": "cmg7c0n1t0001qz8k2v5x9abc",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "formId": null,
    "listIds": ["cmg7l1st00002qz8kfe4w1xyz"],
    "topicIds": ["cmg7t0p1c0003qz8k7h2d4pqr"],
    "confirmedAt": "2026-10-06T14:05:40.000Z"
  }
}
```

`formId` is `null` when the subscription came from the Subscriptions API.

### contact.unsubscribed [#contactunsubscribed]

The recipient unsubscribed from everything, from one list, or from one topic. Fires even when the recipient is not one of your contacts (for example an unsubscribe from API-sent marketing mail).

```json
{
  "eventType": "contact.unsubscribed",
  "messageId": "a4d9c7e1-5f2b-4c8a-b3e6-7d1f0a9c2e55",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-07T09:12:03.000Z",
  "recipient": "jane@example.com",
  "details": {
    "category": "cmg7t0p1c0003qz8k7h2d4pqr",
    "contactEmail": "jane@example.com",
    "contactId": "cmg7c0n1t0001qz8k2v5x9abc",
    "scope": "topic",
    "listId": null,
    "topicId": "cmg7t0p1c0003qz8k7h2d4pqr",
    "method": "preference_center",
    "campaignId": null,
    "reason": null
  }
}
```

| `details` field | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `contactEmail`  | The address that unsubscribed                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `contactId`     | The contact, or `null` when the address is not a contact                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `scope`         | `all` (no marketing mail at all), `list` or `topic`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `listId`        | The list left, for `scope: "list"`                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `topicId`       | The topic opted out of, for `scope: "topic"`                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `method`        | `one_click` (mailbox provider button, or the button on NorthRelay's hosted unsubscribe page), `link` (your own unsubscribe page via `POST /unsubscribe`), `preference_center`, `api`, `dashboard`, `platform_settings` or `complaint` |
| `campaignId`    | The campaign the unsubscribe came from, when known                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `reason`        | Free text, when given                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `category`      | Legacy alias of `topicId`, kept for existing consumers                                                                                                                                                                                |

### list.member\_added and list.member\_removed [#listmember_added-and-listmember_removed]

A contact joined or left a list. `list.member_removed` fires both when a recipient unsubscribes from a list (or from a topic the list is tagged with) and when you remove a member.

```json
{
  "eventType": "list.member_removed",
  "messageId": "c2e7f1a0-8d3b-4a6c-9e5f-1b2d3c4e5f60",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-07T09:12:03.000Z",
  "recipient": "jane@example.com",
  "details": {
    "listId": "cmg7l1st00002qz8kfe4w1xyz",
    "contactId": "cmg7c0n1t0001qz8k2v5x9abc",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "source": "UNSUBSCRIBE"
  }
}
```

`source` is the subscription source (`FORM`, `API`, `IMPORT`, `PREFERENCE_CENTER`, `PLATFORM_SIGNUP`, `DASHBOARD`), or `UNSUBSCRIBE` when the recipient left by unsubscribing. Owner removals through the API use `API`.

### email.opened and email.clicked [#emailopened-and-emailclicked]

A person opened a message or clicked a tracked link. Opens and clicks classified as bots (security scanners, link prefetchers, privacy proxies) are not sent. They fire for campaign mail and for API mail with tracking: marketing-stream API mail is tracked by default (opt out with `track: false`), transactional API mail only with `track: true`.

```json
{
  "eventType": "email.clicked",
  "messageId": "e9f8a7b6-c5d4-4e3f-a2b1-0c9d8e7f6a5b",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-07T10:20:45.000Z",
  "recipient": "jane@example.com",
  "details": {
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "contactId": null,
    "campaignId": null,
    "trackingId": "3f6b2c1e-9a8d-4e7f-b6a5-c4d3e2f1a0b9",
    "url": "https://yourapp.com/pricing",
    "userAgent": "Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 18_0 like Mac OS X)",
    "engagementType": "HUMAN"
  }
}
```

| `details` field           | Description                                           |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `email`                   | Recipient address                                     |
| `contactId`, `campaignId` | Set for campaign mail                                 |
| `trackingId`              | Set for API mail: the tracking id of the sent message |
| `url`                     | The clicked link (`email.clicked` only)               |
| `userAgent`               | Client user agent, or `null`                          |
| `engagementType`          | Always `HUMAN`                                        |

For API mail, `email.opened` fires once per message and recipient; repeat opens are not sent. Clicks fire every time. For campaign mail every human open is sent.

***

## Signature Verification [#signature-verification]

Every webhook request includes an `X-NorthRelay-Signature` header containing an HMAC-SHA256 signature computed from the raw request body and your webhook secret.

**Always verify signatures** to ensure requests originate from NorthRelay and have not been tampered with.

### Verification Algorithm [#verification-algorithm]

1. Extract the `X-NorthRelay-Signature` header value
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your webhook `secret` as the key
3. Compare the computed signature with the header value using a timing-safe comparison

### Node.js Example [#nodejs-example]

```typescript
import crypto from "crypto";

function verifyWebhookSignature(
  body: string,
  signature: string,
  secret: string
): boolean {
  const computed = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(body, "utf8")
    .digest("hex");

  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(computed, "hex"),
    Buffer.from(signature, "hex")
  );
}

// In your webhook handler:
app.post("/webhooks/northrelay", (req, res) => {
  const signature = req.headers["x-northrelay-signature"] as string;
  const rawBody = req.body; // must be the raw string, not parsed JSON

  if (!verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, signature, process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!)) {
    return res.status(401).json({ error: "Invalid signature" });
  }

  const event = JSON.parse(rawBody);
  // Process event...
  res.status(200).json({ received: true });
});
```

### Python Example [#python-example]

```python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_webhook_signature(body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    computed = hmac.new(
        secret.encode("utf-8"),
        body,
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(computed, signature)

# In your webhook handler (Flask):
@app.route("/webhooks/northrelay", methods=["POST"])
def handle_webhook():
    signature = request.headers.get("X-NorthRelay-Signature")
    if not verify_webhook_signature(request.data, signature, WEBHOOK_SECRET):
        return {"error": "Invalid signature"}, 401

    event = request.get_json()
    # Process event...
    return {"received": True}, 200
```

***

## Retry Policy [#retry-policy]

If your endpoint does not respond with a `2xx` status code within 10 seconds, NorthRelay retries the delivery:

| Attempt   | Delay      |
| --------- | ---------- |
| 1st retry | 30 seconds |
| 2nd retry | 2 minutes  |
| 3rd retry | 15 minutes |
| 4th retry | 1 hour     |
| 5th retry | 4 hours    |

After 5 failed retries, the event is marked as failed. Failed events are visible in **Dashboard > Webhooks > Event Log** for 30 days.

### Best Practices [#best-practices]

1. **Respond quickly.** Return `200` immediately and process the event asynchronously. Do not perform heavy work in the request handler.
2. **Handle duplicates.** Deduplicate on `eventType`, `messageId` and `recipient`. The same event may be delivered more than once, and a contact change can arrive before or after a related `list.*` event; read the current state with `GET /subscriptions/{email}` when order matters.
3. **Verify signatures.** Always validate the `X-NorthRelay-Signature` header.
4. **Use HTTPS.** Webhook URLs must use HTTPS. HTTP endpoints are rejected.
5. **Log failures.** Monitor your webhook endpoint health in the dashboard.


# Billing FAQ



# Billing FAQ [#billing-faq]

## Plan Changes [#plan-changes]

### Can I switch plans at any time? [#can-i-switch-plans-at-any-time]

Yes. You can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time from **Dashboard > Billing > Change Plan**.

* **Upgrades** take effect immediately. You get instant access to the new tier's features and sending limits.
* **Downgrades** take effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You keep your current features until then.

### Is my billing prorated when I upgrade? [#is-my-billing-prorated-when-i-upgrade]

Yes. When you upgrade mid-cycle, you are charged the prorated difference for the remaining days in your billing period. For example, if you upgrade from Micro ($12/mo) to Pro ($29/mo) halfway through your cycle, you pay approximately $8.50 for the remaining half-month.

### Is my billing prorated when I downgrade? [#is-my-billing-prorated-when-i-downgrade]

No. Downgrades take effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You are not refunded for the remaining days on your current plan, but you retain full access to your current tier's features until the cycle ends.

### What happens to my custom domains if I downgrade? [#what-happens-to-my-custom-domains-if-i-downgrade]

Custom domains are a Starter+ feature, and each tier allows a different number (1 / 2 / 5 / 20). If you downgrade to Free, or to a tier with fewer domains than you have:

* Domains above the new limit are **deactivated** (not deleted) at the end of the billing cycle
* Emails from a deactivated domain are rejected with `FORBIDDEN_SENDER`; use a remaining verified domain or your NorthRelay system subdomain instead
* Your domain configuration is preserved -- if you upgrade again, your domains reactivate without needing to re-verify DNS

### What happens to my webhooks if I downgrade? [#what-happens-to-my-webhooks-if-i-downgrade]

Webhooks are a Starter+ feature with a per-tier count (1 / 3 / 10 / unlimited). If you downgrade below your current count:

* Webhook endpoints above the new limit are **paused** at the end of the billing cycle
* No events are delivered while paused
* Webhook configurations are preserved -- upgrading reactivates them

### What happens to my team members if I downgrade below Pro? [#what-happens-to-my-team-members-if-i-downgrade-below-pro]

Team members are a Pro+ feature. If you downgrade:

* Team member access is **revoked** at the end of the billing cycle
* Team member accounts are preserved -- upgrading restores their access

## Quotas & Limits [#quotas--limits]

### What happens if I exceed my monthly email quota? [#what-happens-if-i-exceed-my-monthly-email-quota]

When you reach your monthly sending limit:

* Additional send requests return an error: `451 4.7.1 Rate limit exceeded`
* The API returns a `QuotaExceededError` with a clear message
* Already-queued and in-progress emails continue to deliver
* Your dashboard shows a warning when you reach 80% of your quota
* Your quota resets at the start of your next billing cycle

You can upgrade your plan at any time to get a higher quota immediately.

### Do unused emails roll over to the next month? [#do-unused-emails-roll-over-to-the-next-month]

No. Email quotas reset at the start of each billing cycle. Unused emails do not carry over.

### Is there an overage option instead of upgrading? [#is-there-an-overage-option-instead-of-upgrading]

Not currently. If you regularly exceed your quota, upgrading to the next tier is the recommended approach. Enterprise plans can include custom quota arrangements -- [contact sales](mailto:sales@northrelay.ca).

## Payments [#payments]

### What payment methods do you accept? [#what-payment-methods-do-you-accept]

NorthRelay accepts Visa, Mastercard, and American Express credit and debit cards. All payments are processed securely through Stripe.

### What currency are charges in? [#what-currency-are-charges-in]

All charges are in **CAD** (Canadian dollars). Prices are tax-exclusive; GST/HST and, for Québec, QST are added at checkout.

### When am I charged? [#when-am-i-charged]

You are charged on the same day each month, based on the date you first subscribed. For example, if you signed up on March 15, you are charged on the 15th of each month.

### What if my payment fails? [#what-if-my-payment-fails]

If a payment fails:

1. You receive an email notification
2. Stripe automatically retries after 3 days, then again after 5 days
3. If all retries fail, your account is downgraded to the Free tier
4. You can resolve it at any time by updating your payment method and retrying

No data is lost during a payment failure. Your account, domains, templates, and contacts are all preserved.

### Can I pay annually? [#can-i-pay-annually]

Annual billing is not currently available for self-service plans. Enterprise customers can arrange annual billing -- [contact sales](mailto:sales@northrelay.ca).

## Refunds [#refunds]

### What is your refund policy? [#what-is-your-refund-policy]

NorthRelay offers a **14-day money-back guarantee** on your first payment for any paid plan. If you are not satisfied within 14 days of your first charge, contact support for a full refund.

After the 14-day window:

* Monthly charges are **not refundable** once the billing cycle has started
* Downgrades take effect at the end of the cycle (no partial refund)
* If there is a service issue on NorthRelay's end (outage, billing error), refunds or credits are handled on a case-by-case basis

### How do I request a refund? [#how-do-i-request-a-refund]

Email [support@northrelay.ca](mailto:support@northrelay.ca) with your account email and the reason for your request. Refund requests within the 14-day window are processed within 5-10 business days.

## Free Tier [#free-tier]

### What are the Free tier limitations? [#what-are-the-free-tier-limitations]

The Free tier includes:

* 3,000 emails per month
* Sends from a NorthRelay system subdomain only (no custom domains)
* No inbox access
* Full API and SDK access
* No webhooks, campaigns or team features

There is no time limit on the Free tier. You can use it indefinitely.

### Do I need a credit card for the free tier? [#do-i-need-a-credit-card-for-the-free-tier]

No. The Free tier requires no credit card and no payment information.

## Enterprise [#enterprise]

### How does Enterprise pricing work? [#how-does-enterprise-pricing-work]

Enterprise pricing is custom based on your requirements:

* **Volume:** Sending limits above the Scale tier
* **Support:** Priority support with guaranteed response times, dedicated account manager
* **Compliance:** Custom SLA, data processing agreements, security reviews

[Contact sales](mailto:sales@northrelay.ca) for a quote.

### Can I get a dedicated IP? [#can-i-get-a-dedicated-ip]

No. NorthRelay sends all mail from one protected IP and does not offer dedicated IPs on any plan. For typical volumes a warm, continuously monitored IP with a strict sender policy (verified domains only, one-click unsubscribe, automatic bounce and complaint suppression) outperforms a cold dedicated IP, which needs weeks of careful warm-up before mailbox providers trust it. See [Sending Infrastructure](/docs/features/two-pool-system).

### Do you offer non-profit or startup discounts? [#do-you-offer-non-profit-or-startup-discounts]

Contact [sales@northrelay.ca](mailto:sales@northrelay.ca) to discuss special pricing for qualified non-profits and early-stage startups.

## Related [#related]

* [Plans & Pricing](/docs/billing/plans) for detailed tier comparison
* [Invoices](/docs/billing/invoices) for payment and receipt management


# Invoices



# Invoices [#invoices]

NorthRelay uses Stripe for all billing and payment processing. Your invoices, payment methods, and billing history are managed through the dashboard.

## Accessing Invoices [#accessing-invoices]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing**
2. Click the **Invoices** tab
3. Your invoice history is displayed in reverse chronological order

Each row shows:

* Invoice date
* Invoice number
* Amount
* Status (Paid, Pending, Failed)
* A link to view or download

## Invoice Details [#invoice-details]

Each invoice includes:

| Field              | Description                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Invoice Number** | Unique identifier (e.g., `INV-2026-0042`)                 |
| **Date**           | The billing date                                          |
| **Due Date**       | When payment is due (typically the same day for auto-pay) |
| **Plan**           | Your current tier and billing period                      |
| **Amount**         | The charge for the billing period                         |
| **Tax**            | Applicable taxes (if any, based on your billing address)  |
| **Total**          | Final amount charged                                      |
| **Status**         | Paid, Pending, or Failed                                  |
| **Payment Method** | The card or method used for payment                       |

## Downloading Receipts [#downloading-receipts]

To download a PDF receipt:

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing > Invoices**
2. Click **Download** on the invoice row
3. A PDF receipt downloads to your device

Receipts include all information needed for expense reporting and accounting: invoice number, date, line items, tax breakdown, and payment confirmation.

## Payment Methods [#payment-methods]

NorthRelay accepts:

* **Credit cards** -- Visa, Mastercard, American Express
* **Debit cards** -- Visa Debit, Mastercard Debit

All payment processing is handled securely by Stripe. NorthRelay never stores your full card number.

### Adding a Payment Method [#adding-a-payment-method]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing**
2. Click **Payment Methods**
3. Click **Add Payment Method**
4. Enter your card details
5. Click **Save**

### Updating Your Default Payment Method [#updating-your-default-payment-method]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing > Payment Methods**
2. Click **Set as Default** on the card you want to use
3. Future charges will use this card

### Removing a Payment Method [#removing-a-payment-method]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing > Payment Methods**
2. Click **Remove** on the card you want to delete
3. Confirm removal

You cannot remove your only payment method while on a paid plan. Add a new method first, then remove the old one.

## Updating Billing Information [#updating-billing-information]

To update your billing name, address, or email (for invoice delivery):

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing**
2. Click **Billing Details**
3. Update your information
4. Click **Save**

Changes apply to future invoices. Past invoices are not retroactively updated.

## Failed Payments [#failed-payments]

If a payment fails:

1. NorthRelay sends an email notification to your account email
2. The invoice status shows as **Failed** in your dashboard
3. Stripe automatically retries the charge after 3 days, then again after 5 days
4. If all retries fail, your account may be downgraded to the Free tier

To resolve a failed payment:

1. Go to **Dashboard > Billing > Payment Methods**
2. Update your payment method or add a new card
3. Click **Retry Payment** on the failed invoice
4. Your service is restored immediately upon successful payment

## Billing Cycle [#billing-cycle]

* Billing is monthly, charged on the same day each month (based on your signup date)
* If you sign up on the 31st, you are charged on the last day of shorter months
* All amounts are in **USD**
* Invoices are generated at the start of each billing cycle

## Related [#related]

* [Plans & Pricing](/docs/billing/plans) for tier comparison
* [Billing FAQ](/docs/billing/faq) for common questions about billing


# Plans & Pricing



# Plans & Pricing [#plans--pricing]

NorthRelay offers five self-service tiers plus Enterprise. Prices are in **Canadian dollars per month**, tax-exclusive (GST/HST and QST are added at checkout). Sending quotas are **per calendar month** and reset on the 1st. The Micro plan includes a 14-day free trial.

| **Emails / month**                   | 3,000      | 5,000   | 20,000  | 50,000   | 150,000          | Custom       |
| **Custom domains**                   | --         | 1       | 2       | 5        | 20               | Unlimited    |
| **Inbox (JMAP + IMAP)**              | --         | 1 GB    | 2 GB    | 5 GB     | 20 GB            | 50 GB        |
| **Aliases**                          | --         | 3       | 10      | 25       | Unlimited        | Unlimited    |
| **Inbox users**                      | --         | --      | 1       | 5        | 25               | Unlimited    |

| **Support**                          | Docs       | Email   | Email   | Priority | Priority + Slack | Dedicated AM |
| **Custom SLA**                       | --         | --      | --      | --       | --               | Yes          |

## Included on every plan [#included-on-every-plan]

* **Hosted in Canada, billed in CAD.** Relay, mailbox and dashboard run on Canadian servers.
* **REST API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, OpenAPI spec and an MCP server.**
* **One clean, monitored sending IP.** Only verified sender domains can send; campaigns carry one-click unsubscribe; bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically.
* **Deliverability tooling:** blocklist monitor (13 RBLs), DNS and pre-flight checks, link scanner, reputation score with incident alerts.
* **DMARC and TLS-RPT ingestion** for your domains, attributed to your account.
* **Hourly delivery canary** that sends a real message through the relay and reads back its SPF, DKIM and DMARC verdicts.

## Free [#free]

The Free tier is for testing and evaluation. No credit card required.

* **3,000 emails per month**
* Sends from a NorthRelay system subdomain (`yourname.north-pipe.ca`)
* Full API and SDK access
* No inbox, custom domains, webhooks or team features

**Best for:** Developers evaluating NorthRelay, personal projects, proof-of-concept integrations.

## Starter ($5/month) [#starter-5month]

Your own domain, a small inbox and an API, for less than most hosted mailboxes.

* **5,000 emails per month**
* **1 custom domain** with full SPF/DKIM/DMARC alignment
* Inbox with 1 GB storage, JMAP and IMAP access, 3 aliases
* 1 webhook
* 30-day analytics

**Best for:** Solo developers and small sites that want transactional email and a mailbox on their own domain.

## Micro ($12/month) [#micro-12month]

Adds campaigns and automation. Includes a 14-day free trial.

* **20,000 emails per month**
* 2 custom domains
* Campaigns, templates, scheduling and A/B tests
* Inbox with 2 GB storage, 10 aliases, 1 extra inbox user
* 3 webhooks
* 90-day analytics

**Best for:** Small businesses and newsletters that send both transactional and marketing mail.

## Pro ($29/month) [#pro-29month]

The plan for products and teams.

* **50,000 emails per month**
* 5 custom domains
* **Catch-all** inbox on your domains
* Inbox with 5 GB storage, 25 aliases, 5 inbox users
* 3 team members
* 10 webhooks
* 1-year analytics and 90-day logs
* Priority email support

**Best for:** SaaS products, growing businesses, anyone who needs deliverability guarantees.

## Scale ($79/month) [#scale-79month]

High volume for teams and agencies.

* **150,000 emails per month**
* 20 custom domains
* Inbox with 20 GB storage, unlimited aliases, 25 inbox users
* 10 team members
* Unlimited webhooks
* 1-year log and analytics retention
* Priority support with a shared Slack channel

**Best for:** Agencies, multi-brand senders and marketing teams.

## Enterprise (Custom Pricing) [#enterprise-custom-pricing]

Everything in Scale plus negotiated volume and pacing, SSO/SAML, a custom SLA and migration assistance. Dedicated sending infrastructure is available on request.

[Contact sales](mailto:sales@northrelay.ca) for Enterprise pricing.

## Sending infrastructure [#sending-infrastructure]

All tiers send from the same protected IP (`sovereign.north-pipe.ca`). Plans differ by quota, custom domains, campaigns, inbox size and retention -- never by where your mail comes from.

What keeps that IP clean is enforced on every message: only verified sender domains are accepted, every campaign carries one-click unsubscribe headers, bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically, and an hourly delivery canary confirms mail is landing with SPF, DKIM and DMARC passing.

For details, see [Sending Infrastructure](/docs/features/two-pool-system).

## Feature Gates [#feature-gates]

| Feature                                   | Minimum Tier | Why                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Custom domains, inbox, webhooks           | Starter ($5) | Domain verification and mailbox provisioning have per-account cost    |
| Campaigns, templates, scheduling          | Micro ($12)  | Bulk sending needs suppression, unsubscribe and pacing infrastructure |
| Catch-all, team members, priority support | Pro ($29)    | Multi-user access control and support capacity                        |

## What happens when I reach my quota? [#what-happens-when-i-reach-my-quota]

Sends beyond your monthly quota are rejected with `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (API) or `451 4.7.1 Monthly quota exceeded` (SMTP) until the counter resets on the 1st, or until you upgrade. The dashboard warns you at 80 %.

## How to Upgrade [#how-to-upgrade]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Settings > Billing**
2. Click **Change Plan**
3. Select your new tier
4. Enter payment information (if not already on file)
5. Confirm the upgrade

Upgrades take effect immediately. You get instant access to the new tier's features and sending limits. See the [Billing FAQ](/docs/billing/faq) for proration details.

## How to Downgrade [#how-to-downgrade]

1. Go to **Dashboard > Settings > Billing**
2. Click **Change Plan**
3. Select a lower tier
4. Confirm the downgrade

Downgrades take effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You keep your current tier's features until then. Note that downgrading may disable features (e.g., extra custom domains, webhooks, team members) that are not available on the lower tier.
